context: Az-Zalzalah is commonly counted Madinan in the transmitted lists, though its short hammering cadence made others hold it Makkan, and the scholars record the difference honestly. Its subject needs no dating: the final earthquake, the earth emptying her burdens, the dead and the buried secrets together, and mankind surfacing in scattered groups to be shown, not told about, their deeds.

One sound moment ties it to the Prophet’s ﷺ teaching. Asked about donkeys, whether any revelation covered them, he ﷺ answered that nothing had come down about them except this single, all-embracing verse: whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. He called it al-ayah al-fadhdhah al-jami’ah, the unique, comprehensive verse, a complete law of moral accounting in two lines, and the early community weighed their smallest acts against it.
name_story: The surah is named for az-zalzalah, the violent shaking of its first verse, when the earth is convulsed with her true convulsion. Some books write the title Az-Zilzal, the Earthquake itself; both forms are early, and both name the surah after the sound of its opening.

movements.note: The final quake is the earth’s own, long appointed, and she throws out her burdens, the buried dead and the buried truths, while man asks the last confused question: what is wrong with her.
That day she tells her news, every deed done on her back, because her Lord has inspired her, the silent witness under our feet finally given speech.
Mankind proceeds in separated crowds to be shown their deeds, and the surah closes with the comprehensive law: an atom’s weight of good is seen, an atom’s weight of evil is seen.

themes.d: The ground that hosted every secret act is given a voice. Nothing was done nowhere; every deed had a floor, and the floor will speak.
Mithqala dharrah, the weight of a speck of dust: the surah abolishes the category of deeds that do not count, in both directions.
Liyuraw a’malahum, that they may be shown their deeds: the Day is not a verdict read at a distance but an exhibition each soul walks through.
Burdens thrown out, news told, atoms weighed: the surah is one long unveiling, and its terror or comfort depends entirely on what was hidden.

heart: Az-Zalzalah recited slowly makes the floor under the reciter feel briefly alive, because it is: the surah says the ground you are sitting on is a witness scheduled to testify. What that does to a heart is very precise. Sins one had filed away as too small to matter, and kindnesses one had dismissed as too small to bother with, both walk back into the ledger, because the unit of account here is the dharrah, the atom, the dust-speck in a sunbeam. The Prophet ﷺ told the Companions to guard against the fire even with half a date given in charity, and this surah is the mathematics behind that counsel.

The mercy inside the terror is the symmetry of the last two verses. The same law that guarantees no evil is lost guarantees no good is lost either. The smile, the moved stone, the swallowed retort, the two quiet rak’ahs, prayer units, at night: all of it is seen. For the discouraged doer of small good deeds, this is one of the most consoling passages in the Quran.

passages.why: The verse where the earth herself begins to speak: hear the ground turn witness.
The verse the Prophet ﷺ called uniquely comprehensive: an atom’s weight of good, seen.
Its mirror and warning: an atom’s weight of evil, seen, the end of the category called minor.

connections.why: Al-Qari’ah continues the same Day: the atoms counted here are weighed there, and the scales decide the two homes.
Al-Adiyat ends where this surah lives, with graves overturned and chests unsealed before a Lord fully aware.

virtue.text: The famous report that Az-Zalzalah equals half the Quran is transmitted with a weak chain, and its grade is debated among the scholars, so it should not be taught as established. What is sound is the Prophet’s ﷺ praise of its seventh and eighth verses as the unique, comprehensive verse on recompense.
virtue.src: Tirmidhi 2893, graded weak; the comprehensive verse, Bukhari 2371
